products.name: DaVinci Resolve AI
products.note: Professional video AI; color grading; facial recognition; local processing option

reading.body:
Blackmagic Design embeds AI into professional video tools rather than offering it as a standalone service, with DaVinci Resolve AI providing local processing options for color grading and facial recognition.

The company's strategy reflects a pattern in AI adoption at the infrastructure layer of content production. Rather than requiring cloud connectivity, DaVinci Resolve AI includes local processing, which means compute happens on the user's hardware. For a tool used in broadcast and feature film workflows, this matters because it reduces latency, keeps raw footage from traveling to remote servers, and gives productions control over their data. The choice is architectural: Blackmagic builds hardware first (cameras, switchers, storage, networking devices), then layers AI capabilities into the software that ties these systems together.

The data does not capture whether DaVinci Resolve AI is a revenue driver, how much compute it requires relative to the company's broader product line, or how it performs relative to cloud-based video editing tools. It also does not detail the local processing specifications or whether GPU acceleration is required. The emphasis on high-bandwidth connectivity in recent product announcements suggests the company sees data throughput, not AI inference, as its primary constraint.
